clinicalPearls: Two biologically distinct esophageal cancers arise in the same organ: squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), favoring the upper and mid esophagus, and adenocarcinoma, almost always in the lower esophagus and at the gastroesophageal junction (GEJ); globally SCC predominates while adenocarcinoma now accounts for over 75% of incident U.S./Western European cases.

Because dysphagia and odynophagia are typically not noticed until the lumen is substantially obstructed, most esophageal cancers are locally advanced or metastatic at diagnosis; any patient with these symptoms warrants upper endoscopy with biopsy.

Helicobacter pylori is a major chronic-inflammation driver of gastric cancer, but cancer develops in only a small subset of the roughly half of humans infected; eradication has been shown in prospective trials to lower subsequent gastric cancer risk, supporting treatment of asymptomatic H. pylori in those with a first-degree relative with gastric cancer or a prior early-stage gastric cancer.

Physical findings suggesting advanced/metastatic gastric cancer include left supraclavicular adenopathy (Virchow's node), a periumbilical nodule (Sister Mary Joseph nodule), a palpable rectal-shelf mass (Blumer's shelf), ascites, and an ovarian mass (Krukenberg tumor); more commonly the exam is unrevealing.

Diffuse (signet-cell) gastric cancer may not form a discrete mass or ulcer, instead producing thickened gastric rugae and tracking beneath an intact mucosal surface, so initial superficial biopsies can be falsely negative and EUS-guided deeper biopsy may be required.

Germline CDH1 (e-cadherin) mutation markedly increases risk of the diffuse/signet-cell gastric cancer subtype and also raises lobular breast cancer risk; prophylactic gastrectomy is an option in CDH1 carriers.

Molecular profiling is therapeutically decisive: roughly 20-25% of esophageal/GEJ and about 20% of gastric adenocarcinomas overexpress or amplify HER2/ERBB2, and MSI-high/mismatch-repair-deficient and PD-L1-high (high combined positive score) tumors identify candidates for immune-modulating therapy; NGS plus PD-L1 IHC should be routine in metastatic disease.

Gastric lymphomas (about 3% of gastric malignancies) are extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphomas; the GI tract is the most common extranodal NHL site and the stomach is the most common GI site, with MALT (~40%) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (~55%) being the dominant subtypes.

MALT lymphoma of the stomach is strongly H. pylori-associated, and the stomach accounts for about 35% of all MALT lymphomas; the t(11;18) translocation marks tumors less likely to respond to H. pylori eradication.

GISTs arise from the interstitial cells of Cajal and are driven by activating cKIT (~majority) or PDGFRA mutations; the stomach is the most frequent primary site (~60%), followed by small bowel (~25%); spindle-cell histology predominates (~70%) and KIT expression is found in ~95%.

Small-bowel neoplasms account for only about 3% of GI tumors; in the U.S., neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumors (40-45%) slightly outnumber adenocarcinomas (30-40%), and the duodenum is the most common site (~50%).

EBV is associated with a distinct gastric cancer subtype (identified in roughly 8-10% of gastric cancer patients) and is described as a driver in some esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinomas; current EBV positivity does not by itself change therapeutic options.
harrison.pathophysiology: Esophageal SCC is linked to mucosal injury from alcohol and tobacco (synergistic), ingestion of very hot beverages, areca/betel-nut chewing, chronic achalasia, prior radiation, lye-induced strictures, and Plummer-Vinson (Patterson-Kelly) syndrome; genomically it resembles SCCs of other sites (e.g., head and neck) more than esophageal adenocarcinoma, and HPV is not implicated. Esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma arises in the setting of chronic gastroesophageal reflux producing inflammation and Barrett's metaplasia (glandular gastric-type mucosa extending into the esophagus); progression through dysplasia accumulates TP53 mutations and aneuploidy, with annual risk of progression of Barrett's to cancer about 0.4-0.5%. Gastric adenocarcinoma is predominantly an inflammation-driven malignancy: H. pylori (and the broader gastric microbiome) and ingestion of nitrate-rich smoked/salted/dried foods generate carcinogenic nitrites; the intestinal Lauren subtype associates with H. pylori and atrophic gastritis, while the diffuse subtype (~20%) associates with germline or somatic CDH1 loss. TCGA defines four molecular subtypes (EBV-positive, microsatellite-unstable/hypermutated, genomically stable [diffuse], and chromosomally unstable). The proximal esophagus-GEJ-gastric cardia adenocarcinomas share a similar genomic profile suggesting common driving factors. Gastric MALT lymphoma is driven by chronic antigenic stimulation from H. pylori, with the t(11;18) API1-MALT1 fusion activating NF-kB signaling. GISTs originate from Cajal cells via gain-of-function KIT or PDGFRA mutations.
additionalDifferentials: Reflux esophagitis / Barrett's esophagus without malignancy
Achalasia and other benign esophageal motility/stricture disorders
Gastric adenocarcinoma vs primary gastric lymphoma (treatment differs markedly, so adequate tissue is essential)
Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (submucosal smooth bulging mass)
Metastatic disease to stomach or esophagus from another primary
Small-bowel adenocarcinoma vs neuroendocrine (carcinoid) tumor, lymphoma, or GIST
nonInfectiousMimics: Submucosal benign tumors (lipoma, leiomyoma, neurofibroma, lymphoid nodular hyperplasia)
additionalInvestigations: Upper endoscopy with biopsy to establish histology (deep or repeated biopsies / EUS-guided sampling for suspected diffuse gastric cancer or lymphoma that tracks submucosally)
Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis to assess metastatic disease
FDG-PET/CT (more sensitive than CT for metastases, but may be non-informative in diffuse-type gastric cancer or non-FDG-avid tumors)
Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) to determine depth of tumor penetration (T stage) and regional nodal involvement when no metastatic disease is seen
Staging laparoscopy with peritoneal washing cytology for GEJ/gastric tumors with advanced T stage to detect peritoneal involvement
Bronchoscopy for mid/upper esophageal tumors to exclude tracheobronchial invasion (its presence precludes curative surgery)
Molecular/NGS profiling, PD-L1 IHC, HER2/ERBB2 (IHC/FISH/NGS), and MSI/mismatch-repair-protein testing on metastatic tumors to guide systemic therapy
Plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) when biopsy tissue is insufficient, and as an investigational measure of minimal residual disease
H. pylori status assessment in all gastric lymphoma patients (histology, and if negative, stool antigen or urea breath test); HBV testing before lymphoma therapy
Gallium-68 or copper-64 DOTATATE scan for neuroendocrine tumors; CT/MR enterography and device-assisted enteroscopy or capsule endoscopy for small-bowel neoplasms
Germline genetic testing in small-bowel adenocarcinoma and in patients suspected of hereditary syndromes (CDH1, Lynch, FAP, Peutz-Jeghers, BRCA)
redFlags: New or progressive dysphagia or odynophagia, especially with weight loss
Hematemesis or melena, or unexplained iron-deficiency anemia from occult GI bleeding
Anorexia, early satiety, and unexplained weight loss
Left supraclavicular (Virchow's) node, Sister Mary Joseph periumbilical nodule, Blumer's shelf, ascites, or Krukenberg ovarian mass indicating advanced disease
Dysphagia, odynophagia, or upper abdominal discomfort in a patient under 50, given the rising incidence of early-onset upper GI cancers (symptoms must not be dismissed as benign)
Small-bowel obstruction, perforation, or intussusception as a presentation of small-bowel neoplasm
harrison.prognosis: Esophageal cancer prognosis remains poor overall but is slowly improving; by clinical (pretreatment) AJCC staging, 5-year survival ranges from about 75-82% for stage 0-I down to roughly 5-18% for metastatic (stage IVB) disease, and most U.S. patients present with locally advanced or metastatic disease. For gastric cancer, surgery alone yields about 25% overall 5-year survival, with stage-dependent rates falling from about 90% (stage 0) to roughly 3% for stage IV; multimodality therapy (perioperative chemotherapy plus surgery) improves 5-year survival by about 10-15% over surgery alone (e.g., MAGIC trial 36% vs 23%). Even with modern systemic and immune-modulating therapy, overall survival for stage IV gastric cancer is still only about 12-15 months. Gastric MSI-high tumors had the best outcomes and genomically stable (diffuse)/mesenchymal subtypes the worst in genomic series. Lynch-syndrome-associated small-bowel cancers probably have a better prognosis. For nonmetastatic gastric GIST, resected tumors 2 cm or smaller with a mitotic index of 5% or less carry near-zero progression risk, whereas tumors 10 cm or larger with mitotic index above 5% are moderate-to-high risk.
pitfalls: Falsely reassuring superficial endoscopic biopsies in diffuse-type gastric cancer or gastric lymphoma, which track below the mucosa; adequate deep tissue or EUS-guided sampling is required.
Relying on FDG-PET to exclude disease in diffuse-type gastric cancer, which is often not FDG-avid (PET may be non-informative).
Using tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9) for diagnosis; they are nonspecific and elevated in many cancers, and are better for monitoring response/progression.
Attributing alarm symptoms in patients under 50 to benign illness and delaying diagnostic workup, given rising early-onset upper GI cancer incidence.
Missing tracheobronchial invasion in mid/upper esophageal tumors, which precludes curative surgery, by omitting bronchoscopy.
Treating gastric lymphoma like adenocarcinoma; surgical resection has no role in primary gastric lymphoma and MALT may respond to H. pylori eradication alone, so accurate subtyping is critical.
Assuming a t(11;18)-positive MALT lymphoma will respond to H. pylori eradication; this subgroup is less likely to respond.
Forgetting HBV testing before initiating lymphoma therapy (risk of reactivation).
harrison.severityClassification: Esophageal and gastric cancers are staged with the AJCC TNM system (eighth edition; ninth edition expected 2024), with separate clinical (cTNM, pretreatment), pathologic (pTNM, for patients undergoing initial surgery), and post-neoadjuvant (ypTNM) classifications. The esophageal T stage reflects depth of penetration through the wall (which over most of its course lacks serosa); regional nodal disease is still potentially curable while metastatic disease is generally treated palliatively. Gastric staging similarly progresses from Tis (mucosa-confined, stage 0) through wall penetration and increasing nodal involvement to distant metastasis (stage IV). Gastric lymphomas are NOT staged by TNM; the Lugano system (an Ann Arbor modification) is used: stage I confined to the gastric wall, stage II regional nodal or local-structure involvement, stage III nodes on both sides of the diaphragm, stage IV more extensive nodal or distant/extranodal (including marrow) disease. GIST recurrence risk is stratified by primary tumor size, mitotic index, and GI location. Neuroendocrine tumors are graded 1-3 by Ki-67 positivity, distinct from fully malignant small-/large-cell neuroendocrine carcinomas.
management: Manage through a specialist upper-GI oncology multidisciplinary team after full staging with endoscopy and biopsy, contrast CT, endoscopic ultrasound, FDG-PET and staging laparoscopy for gastro-oesophageal and gastric tumours
Offer endoscopic mucosal resection or submucosal dissection for early T1a mucosal cancers and high-grade dysplasia arising in Barrett's oesophagus
Proceed to radical oesophagectomy or gastrectomy with adequate (D2) lymphadenectomy for resectable locally advanced disease
Give neoadjuvant or perioperative chemotherapy, or neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, for locally advanced oesophageal, junctional and gastric adenocarcinoma to improve resectability and survival
Treat advanced or metastatic disease with platinum-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy, adding trastuzumab for HER2-positive tumours and immune checkpoint inhibitors where indicated
Eradicate Helicobacter pylori and provide palliative luminal stenting, nutritional support with enteral feeding, and analgesia for obstructing or incurable disease
Refer germline CDH1 (E-cadherin) carriers for genetic counselling and consideration of prophylactic total gastrectomy and lobular breast surveillance
